## Problem
A new user needs complete preparation for Windows/WSL2 and native Linux without manually assembling Python, Incus, permissions, networking and browser access. Existing prepare_linux.sh and the Windows WSL bridge are reusable foundations, but do not provide a complete guided host bootstrap.

## Goal and operator contract
Provide two documented preparation commands from an extracted release or repository checkout:
- Windows, elevated PowerShell: `./prepare_windows.ps1 -Distro Ubuntu-24.04` (PowerShell-native invocation documented in the guide).
- Supported native Ubuntu: `./prepare_linux.sh`.
After preparation, `./install.sh` starts TSW in the selected Linux/WSL shell. An optional explicit PowerShell install handoff may delegate to WSL; Windows never runs product Python itself.
These are target contracts, not claims that new capabilities already exist.

## Requirements
- BOOT-01: Read-only inventory, plan and readiness contract with actionable remediation and stable exit states.
- BOOT-02: Windows features, WSL2 distribution and systemd preparation with resumable reboot/restart boundaries.
- BOOT-03: Capacity-aware WSL configuration preserving Windows reserve and existing .wslconfig, wsl.conf and distribution state.
- BOOT-04: Complete host package/Python prerequisite installation on supported native Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu, bootstrapping from a clean host.
- BOOT-05: Safe Incus daemon, current-user access, storage, network and profile initialization; preserve existing unrelated resources.
- BOOT-06: Required kernel/network controls and TSW-scoped access integration, reusing the existing Windows bridge and canonical port registry.
- BOOT-07: Clear preparation-to-install handoff, ordinary non-destructive install on both hosts, explicit reset kept separate.
- BOOT-08: Idempotent reruns, interruption recovery, protected state/evidence and truthful partial-failure reports.
- BOOT-09: Fresh-host, repeated-run and recovery qualification plus concise copyable user instructions.

## Scope and architecture
Extend the existing preparation/installer services through application ports and concrete host/package/configuration adapters. Keep PowerShell and shell entrypoints thin. The user explicitly requests Windows-side preparation; product execution remains Linux/WSL only. Docker Engine and Swarm workloads remain inside Incus-managed nodes.
Supported initial targets: native Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 x86_64 and Windows 11 with a selected Ubuntu WSL2 distribution; publish the exact qualified Windows/WSL/distribution versions. Unsupported targets must be rejected before mutation.
Package preparation may require elevation; Python dependency installation uses a user-owned local venv. No whole-installer sudo, credential logging or implicit global configuration replacement.

## Relationship to existing work
- Reuse completed #427; do not reopen or duplicate its delivered native installer scope.
- Coordinate architecture and current behavioral evidence with #313 and #363.
- Reuse tools/windows/tws-wsl-bridge.ps1 and its ownership/ACL/service lifecycle.
- Coordinate profile-aware resource needs and future service selection with #440 / #444.
- Dedicated DNS servers, Podman, K3s and multi-host provisioning remain owned by their existing EPICs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A clean supported native host and Windows/WSL target can reach installation-ready state through their documented preparation entrypoint, with unavoidable account creation/reboot interactions explicitly guided.
- [ ] Users do not need manual venv/pip steps, Incus YAML editing or undocumented network commands for the supported default path.
- [ ] Dry-run/preflight write no managed host/configuration/state/evidence data.
- [ ] Plans explain package/configuration changes, resource allocation and required restart scope before apply.
- [ ] Capacity adaptation preserves Windows reserve and fails clearly when selected services cannot fit.
- [ ] Existing Incus resources, Linux/WSL configuration, credentials and unrelated host settings survive repeated preparation.
- [ ] Normal install never silently resets managed nodes on either host; destructive reset requires its own exact confirmation.
- [ ] Failures stop dependent stages, preserve redacted evidence and show a concrete next command.
- [ ] WSL restart/address change recovers browser routing through the existing bridge; readiness is distinguished from live service verification.
- [ ] Fresh install, second run, interrupted run/resume and preservation scenarios have exact-SHA live evidence for both host families.
- [ ] Targeted tests and applicable QUALITY.md gates pass; simulation/unit evidence is never reported as live proof.
- [ ] README presents two short entry paths, prerequisites, supported versions, restart expectations, access URLs and recovery.

## Execution and non-goals
Establish the contract first; implement shared Linux foundations and Windows lifecycle/resource preparation; integrate networking and installer handoff; then qualify and document. Actual issue dependencies are recorded in each child.
Follow current AGENTS.md, QUALITY.md and repository completion/verification policy. Issue creation does not authorize live changes to a user's host.
No production/HA promise, arbitrary distribution support, automatic runtime replacement, whole-host reset, generic fleet manager or unverified remote script execution.

## Work breakdown
- [ ] #453 — [BOOT-W01] Define bootstrap command, host plan and readiness contracts
- [ ] #454 — [BOOT-W02] Implement shared Ubuntu package and Python prerequisite bootstrap
- [ ] #455 — [BOOT-W03] Prepare Incus daemon, permissions, storage, network and profiles safely
- [ ] #456 — [BOOT-W04] Implement PowerShell Windows and WSL2 lifecycle preparation
- [ ] #457 — [BOOT-W05] Adapt WSL resources to host capacity and selected service requirements
- [ ] #458 — [BOOT-W06] Complete kernel, firewall and Windows browser-access preparation
- [ ] #459 — [BOOT-W07] Integrate simple preparation-to-install handoff and non-destructive WSL installs
- [ ] #460 — [BOOT-W08] Implement resumable bootstrap state, recovery and protected evidence
- [ ] #461 — [BOOT-W09] Live-qualify fresh hosts, reruns, restarts and recovery on Linux and WSL2
- [ ] #462 — [BOOT-W10] Document two-command installation and audit bootstrap EPIC completion

## Dependency sequence

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["W01: Contracts"] --> B["W02: Linux packages and Python"]
  B --> C["W03: Incus initialization"]
  A --> D["W04: Windows and WSL lifecycle"]
  D --> E["W05: WSL resources"]
  C --> F["W06: Network and browser access"]
  E --> F
  B --> G["W08: Resume and recovery"]
  C --> G
  D --> G
  F --> H["W07: Installation handoff"]
  H --> I["W09: Live qualification"]
  G --> I
  I --> J["W10: Documentation and audit"]
```

All ten work packages (#453–#462) are linked as native GitHub sub-issues of this EPIC, ordered BOOT-W01 through BOOT-W10. Implementation dependencies remain specified in each child issue.

## Parent and goal
Parent: #452 — Complete Windows/WSL2 and Native Linux Bootstrap with Simple Installation Commands.
Work package: **BOOT-W04**, execution position 4/10.
Requirements: **BOOT-02**.

## Dependencies
- #453 — BOOT-W01

## Scope
- Add thin prepare_windows.ps1 for elevated Windows preparation; validate Windows/architecture/virtualization prerequisites.
- Prepare required Windows features and WSL2; select/install an explicitly named supported Ubuntu distribution without guessing between existing distributions.
- Merge systemd setting into wsl.conf while preserving other sections; verify PID 1.
- Guide unavoidable initial Linux-account creation, reboot and restart steps; do not store account passwords.
- Return explicit restart-required status and support rerunning the same command to continue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] BOOT-W04-AC1: Clean Windows and existing WSL paths reach the requested WSL2/systemd baseline.
- [ ] BOOT-W04-AC2: Missing elevation, virtualization or unsupported distribution reports precise blocker.
- [ ] BOOT-W04-AC3: No distribution unregister, implicit conversion/reset or changes to unrelated distributions.
- [ ] BOOT-W04-AC4: Reboot-required work cannot be reported as complete; rerun resumes safely.

## Verification and completion
Map acceptance IDs to meaningful tests and redacted evidence. Follow current AGENTS.md, QUALITY.md and repository completion/verification policies. Keep shell/PowerShell entrypoints thin, reuse application services/ports and existing bridge/provider configuration. This task explicitly includes Windows-side preparation where applicable; product execution remains Linux/WSL.
Cover plan/apply consent, preservation, rerun and bounded failure behavior. Preflight/dry-run must not write host/configuration/state/evidence. Live claims require an explicitly authorized recoverable target and exact committed SHA/host/version/commands/exit codes; unit/mock/skipped/stale evidence is not a live pass. #452 creation does not authorize live host mutation.
Do not duplicate completed #427, distributed DNS, K3s, Podman or multi-host provisioning. Coordinate service-selection/resource semantics with #440/#444.

## Three Amigos refinement: resolve the W04/W09 qualification dependency

Review date: 2026-10-04. This refinement specifies implementation work; it is not an implemented capability, an accepted repository ADR, live consent or version qualification.

### Problem and architectural decision required before implementation

The BOOT-W01 bootstrap contract blocks Windows-affecting mutation for unknown/unqualified Windows-build/WSL-version combinations. W09 supplies exact-version live qualification, but depends transitively on W04. Requiring W09 qualification before any W04 qualification run creates a dependency cycle. An empty qualification allowlist preserves safety but cannot deliver AC1.

Before product edits, record an independently reviewed, narrowly accepted W04 ADR and synchronize `documentation/contracts/bootstrap.md`, the proposed bootstrap ADR and the W02 amendment's Windows-gate wording. Preserve ADR history. Acceptance must cover the Windows feature/WSL/distro/systemd preparation boundary and the limited qualification exception below. Do not silently relax the existing gate or invent qualified versions. Root architecture owner integrates Requirement, System Architect, Python Automation, Tester, DevOps and Security findings. The repository contract remains authoritative until those changes are accepted.

### Two target states and a bounded qualification path

- **Candidate target:** a precisely specified Windows 11 x86_64 / WSL / explicitly selected Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 x86_64 combination, eligible only for development and explicitly authorized qualification. Candidate criteria and tool/package sources must be sourced from official documentation and recorded in the ADR/configuration. Candidate is not qualified or release-supported merely because unit tests pass.
- **Qualified target:** an exact observed combination with applicable committed-SHA, host/build/WSL/distro/kernel, commands, exits and redacted live evidence reviewed by W09. Qualification is scoped to the recorded scenario/capability and applicable implementation revision; stale or unrelated evidence cannot qualify a new candidate automatically.
- Ordinary Apply remains fail-closed for unqualified/unknown targets. Introduce a separate, explicit **`-QualificationRun`** mode for the selected candidate only. It is not a generic force flag. Require both this mode and fresh per-invocation preparation consent; `-ApproveApply` alone never bypasses qualification. Execution additionally requires separate operator authorization for an identified disposable/restorable host, the exact selected distro, recovery method/snapshot and bounded planned actions. An issue edit, a local environment file, or a saved approval never grants that authorization.
- The qualification plan must name the exact candidate, committed revision, selected distro/default ordinary account when available, source/version and immutable identity of installation artifacts, approved actions, verification probes, deadlines, restart scopes and preservation rules. Reject missing/mismatched authorization context, unsupported/unknown facts, ambiguous distro selection, unsafe configuration ownership or changed plans before mutation. Reruns reobserve state and require fresh consent; approvals do not survive a restart.
- Distinguish **observed absence** from **unreadable/unknown facts**. A clean host with no WSL/distro/account is an explicit planned stage sequence, not a fabricated existing version or identity. Observe and validate Windows/virtualization candidate eligibility and the reviewed installation source first; observe installed WSL facts before dependent distro work, then observe the selected distro's actual OS/architecture/account before Linux configuration. Newly observable facts/actions require a fresh plan and consent. Existing WSL1 selections block; never implicitly convert them.
- Read-only modes never start a stopped selected distro or enable/start Windows/WSL services. Report unavailable Linux facts as UNKNOWN with an operator start command; do not probe by starting it. Read-only preflight/dry-run/help never acquire mutation authority or write host/configuration/state/evidence. `-QualificationRun` cannot turn a read-only mode into Apply. Unsupported flag combinations block before probes/mutation; help performs no probes. JSON never prompts.

### Capability, restart and preservation boundaries

W04 owns only Windows feature/WSL/selected-distro/systemd lifecycle readiness. Keep the root PowerShell entrypoint thin and separate planning/orchestration from scoped host adapters; product Python runs only in Linux/WSL. The accepted ADR must specify a dependency-light PowerShell preparation module with injectable inventory, bounded command and protected-evidence adapters as the pre-Linux owner/test seam. The root script delegates to that module; after Linux facts are verified, reuse the existing dependency-light Linux preparation owners. Existing bridge-specific Windows command ports are not a replacement for this pre-Linux boundary. The module is planned scope, not an existing capability; do not require Python on Windows or an existing distro merely to show help/plan or enable Windows prerequisites.

Preserve AC3: no unregister, implicit conversion/reset, distro replacement, guessed account, stored password or unrelated distro modification. Systemd changes merge only the selected distro's `wsl.conf` boot key and preserve unrelated sections/settings and ownership. Observe PID 1 after the operator restarts the selected distro. Account creation/default-account selection remains operator-guided; absent/root default account blocks dependent Linux configuration rather than making up a user. Stop for symlink/ownership conflicts or ambiguous configuration; do not overwrite blindly.

Test successful-but-reboot-pending native command results, preserved global/default-distro settings and captured native output as well as nonzero failures. Restart scope is explicit: selected-distro restart, WSL-wide shutdown, Windows reboot or account/login steps are disclosed before consent and left to the operator. Never automatically reboot Windows or shut down unrelated distributions. Return `RESTART_REQUIRED` (exit 3), not READY, while restart/account steps remain. Resume by rerunning the same command and reinventorying. Partial failure/uncertain mutation stops dependents and returns the contract's PARTIAL/FAILED/timeout/interruption result with safe recovery guidance; no blanket rollback/reset.

Do not present the W04 lifecycle baseline as aggregate installation READY. Keep preparation capability status, target qualification and live verification as separate fields. A W04 capability may be READY only after verified lifecycle completion; aggregate `preparation_ready` stays false while qualification or W05/W06/W07 prerequisites remain incomplete. `services_verified` remains false. W05 owns resource adaptation, W06 kernel/network/browser preparation and existing bridge integration, W07 installation handoff, W08 shared durable recovery records, W09 integrated live qualification. Reuse existing fixed profiles/canonical sources and bridge ownership; no second service catalog, firewall/portproxy owner or resumability engine. W04 must still safely resume from observed state before W08 exists.

W04 owns minimal protected Windows-side apply evidence before any feature/WSL mutation: validate owner-controlled storage and restrictive ACLs without writes during read-only planning; after approval prepare/verify the protected store before the first host mutation. Refuse symlinks/reparse-point redirection and foreign ownership. Atomically record safe before/after observations, revision, stage/action IDs, confirmed/uncertain effects, restart boundary and exits. Evidence failure before host mutation blocks it; failure after mutation returns PARTIAL. W08 later integrates shared durable records; W04 must not defer these safeguards. Record approval facts only as non-executable audit evidence, never reusable consent.

Candidate policy must name the installation channel, intended version, artifact format and required tool/command capabilities; do not implicitly install a default distro or perform an uncontrolled latest-version update. Preserve the Windows default distro and unrelated global defaults. The ADR must define missing systemd-package handling through the existing W02 package owner rather than a competing W04 package service. Verify official artifact origin and applicable signature/hash/integrity checks before execution; source/version alone is insufficient. Unknown or mismatched artifact identity blocks dependent actions and invalidates consent. Validate distro/account/configuration input and pass structured arguments, never interpolated shell or PowerShell expressions. Capture native DISM/WSL output so JSON remains one envelope; do not expose credentials/raw output in shared evidence.

### Acceptance additions and verification mapping

Original AC1–AC4 remain in scope; no live acceptance is silently reassigned or reduced. Split AC1 evidence into **AC1-LOCAL** (deterministic mocked capability behavior) and **AC1-LIVE** (actual clean-Windows and existing-selected-WSL results). W04 can publish an independently audited `LOCAL_IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE` checkpoint for downstream integration after local requirements pass. AC1-LIVE remains OPEN in this issue, initially `LIVE_CONSENT_MISSING`, until W09 links applicable scenario-specific evidence. Keep #456 INCOMPLETE/open while that required evidence is absent; local completion does not mean issue closure. Downstream work consumes the reviewed committed implementation checkpoint, not closure of #456, so this creates no reverse W09-before-W04 implementation dependency.

| Acceptance ID | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| BOOT-W04-AC1 | Meaningful mocked clean-host and existing-selected-WSL stage sequences reach the requested WSL2/systemd capability only after observed verification. W09 separately executes both scenarios on an authorized recoverable target. |
| BOOT-W04-AC2 | Tests for missing elevation/virtualization, unsupported OS/architecture/release, unreadable facts, ambiguous selection, WSL1 and absent/root default account; precise stage/cause/next action. |
| BOOT-W04-AC3 | Before/after fixtures prove selected-only changes, merged `wsl.conf`, preserved unrelated sections/distributions, no unregister/conversion/reset, no password storage. |
| BOOT-W04-AC4 | Reboot/distro/account boundaries, rerun after each boundary, interrupted/partial attempts and observed no-op reruns; pending restart cannot produce READY. |
| BOOT-W04-AC5 | Accepted narrow ADR and synchronized contract resolve the cycle; candidate/qualified states are explicit and source-backed; ordinary Apply blocks unqualified targets. |
| BOOT-W04-AC6 | Qualification mode requires explicit mode, separate identified-target authorization and exact-plan consent; official artifact integrity and structured argument safety are tested. Missing, mismatched, expired/reused consent or changed target/configuration/source/action blocks. Authorization is never persisted for reuse or inferred; redacted evidence may record the fact of approval without becoming executable consent. |
| BOOT-W04-AC7 | Help requires no elevation/Python/probes; preflight/dry-run are no-write and never start a stopped distro/services; JSON is one nonprompting envelope; invalid mode combinations fail before probes/mutation. |
| BOOT-W04-AC8 | Protected evidence preflight/writes, ACL/ownership/reparse-point conflicts and before/after effects are tested. All probes/actions have positive finite timeouts and explicit finite retry budgets; failure/interruption/timeout stops dependents, retains confirmed/uncertain effects and reports safe next steps. |
| BOOT-W04-AC9 | No W04 capability result implies aggregate installation/service readiness or version qualification; live results and optional gates use canonical policy states. |

### Requirement matrix for implementation handoff

Every row is PLANNED / OPEN / NOT IMPLEMENTED at this refinement; this is a review matrix, not implementation evidence. Populate exact file/test references before implementation approval and then attach executed evidence; acceptance IDs above are stable.

| Requirement | Scope / proposed owner | Verification / acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W04-R01 | BOOT-02 and #452 traceability; dependency on delivered #453; root integration owner | Dependency/source inventory; AC5 |
| W04-R02 | Thin root `prepare_windows.ps1`; dependency-light pre-Linux PowerShell module and adapters; Python only Linux/WSL | Architecture/import checks and executable PowerShell behavior harness; AC1-LOCAL/AC7 |

| W04-R06 | Selected `wsl.conf` merge and observed systemd PID 1 after operator restart | Preservation/conflict/PID1 fixtures; AC1-LOCAL/AC3/AC4 |
| W04-R07 | Account creation/login/reboot/distro restart guidance; no passwords stored | Guided boundary and redaction tests; AC3/AC4 |
| W04-R08 | Explicit restart result, observed rerun/no-op/partial/interruption recovery | Status/exit/rerun tests; AC4/AC8 |
| W04-R09 | No unregister, conversion, reset, replacement or unrelated distro mutation | Mutation-call traps and before/after preservation; AC3 |

| W04-R12 | Qualification-only mode with separate recoverable-target authorization; ordinary Apply fail-closed | Missing/mismatched authorization, stale plan and invalid mode tests; AC6 |
| W04-R13 | Official reviewed artifacts, immutable identity/integrity and validated structured command arguments | Artifact drift/integrity/injection fixtures; AC6/AC8 |
| W04-R14 | Protected Windows evidence before Linux/W08; ownership/ACL/redaction/atomic effect records | Storage refusal, post-mutation evidence failure and secret-leak tests; AC8 |
| W04-R15 | Bounded calls/retries, dependent-stage stop, no automatic destructive rollback | Timeout/interruption/partial/failed probes and effect mapping; AC8 |
| W04-R16 | Capability versus aggregate readiness, live and external states | Result/JSON/console assertions; AC9 |
| W04-R17 | Reuse provider/bridge/profile sources; coordinate #440/#444; preserve W05–W09 ownership and excluded #427/DNS/K3s/Podman/multi-host scope | Owner/source inventory and architecture review; AC5/AC9 |
| W04-R18 | Meaningful focused PowerShell tests and Linux/WSL QUALITY gate; independent completion audit; six issue evidence files | Actual commands/evidence review; AC1–AC9 local mappings |
| W04-R19 | Exact-SHA recoverable-host clean/existing/rerun/restart/recovery live results, separately authorized and executed by W09 | AC1-LIVE stays OPEN until linked applicable redacted live evidence |

Maintain and extend this full requirement matrix before implementation, including every original requirement and this amendment. Maintain all six required issue evidence files under `.tiny-swarm/evidence/issue-456/`; include the ADR/review decision, requirement-to-test mappings, actual command results and remaining risks. Independent audit is required before publishing LOCAL_IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE; issue DONE additionally requires AC1-LIVE evidence. Do not mark live qualification complete from mocked, skipped, stale or dirty-source evidence.

Verification: focused mocked lifecycle/PowerShell adapter tests plus `python3 tools/quality_gate.py quality` under Linux/WSL are APPLICABLE_LOCAL. Require an executable PowerShell syntax/behavior harness for the pre-Linux planner/adapters/core lifecycle. Missing runtime or skipped core behavior tests leaves the affected local acceptance INCOMPLETE; Python tests or text matching do not substitute for PowerShell lifecycle execution. Windows/WSL qualification is APPLICABLE_LIVE / LIVE_CONSENT_MISSING until separate operator authorization exists; then record exact state-specific results. Browser/Selenium is NOT_APPLICABLE for W04 alone because browser routing and services are unchanged; reassess in W06/W07/W09. External CI/SonarQube status follows publication policy and must be observed or explicitly unavailable, never inferred from local quality.

### Dependency and completion decision

Keep the forward dependency: `W01 -> accepted W04 decision -> W04 local implementation -> W05/W06/W07/W08 integration -> W09 live qualification`. W09 may exercise the bounded qualification path before ordinary Apply is released; do not add a W09-before-W04 implementation prerequisite. W09 evidence enables only the applicable qualified combinations, not a blanket allowlist.

This remains aligned with EPIC #452: complete Windows preparation with explicit unavoidable interactions, preservation, simple eventual commands and exact-version live evidence. It does not reopen #427 or authorize DNS, K3s, Podman, multi-host provisioning, installation/reset, capacity adaptation or browser-route implementation in W04.

Independent review findings (2026-10-04):

# Parent

[EPIC 03 — Harden Architecture Boundaries and Decompose Orchestration Hotspots](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/issues/313)

## Context

Tiny Swarm World currently requires a reliable and reproducible installation path for a **native Linux host**. The installation workflow must not depend on WSL-specific assumptions and should provide a clean operator-facing entry point for preparing and installing Tiny Swarm World on a supported Linux machine.

The installer must respect the architecture boundaries defined by EPIC #313: orchestration logic should remain separated from platform detection, package/runtime installation, configuration, validation, and lifecycle execution.

## Goal

Provide a production-oriented native Linux installation script that prepares the host, validates prerequisites, installs required dependencies, configures Tiny Swarm World, and starts the selected runtime/profile in a deterministic and auditable way.

Example operator entry point:

```bash
./install.sh
```

or:

```bash
curl -fsSL <installer-url> | bash
```

The implementation should prefer a repository-local script for auditable installation and only expose remote bootstrap execution when its integrity and security model are clearly documented.

## Scope

### Platform detection

The installer must:

- detect that it is running on native Linux
- distinguish supported distributions where necessary
- detect architecture (`x86_64`, potentially `arm64` if supported)
- reject unsupported operating systems explicitly
- avoid WSL-specific execution paths
- provide actionable diagnostics when prerequisites are missing

Supported host baseline for this issue's live acceptance (operator amendment, 2026-09-27):

- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, including a clean first installation and safe second run
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS remains in the installer allowlist and local regression matrix; its live qualification is separate from this issue's required E2E run
- Debian-compatible distributions may be supported when verified by tests

### Preflight checks

Before any mutating operation, validate at minimum:

- supported Linux distribution/version
- CPU architecture
- minimum CPU resources
- minimum RAM
- minimum free disk space
- root/sudo availability
- network connectivity where required
- DNS/network configuration prerequisites
- required ports
- filesystem permissions
- repository/install target permissions
- required kernel/runtime capabilities
- absence or explicit handling of conflicting container runtimes/services

The preflight must fail fast and clearly identify the blocking condition.

### Dependency installation

The installer should install or verify the dependencies required by the selected Tiny Swarm World profile.

Examples may include:

- Docker Engine / Docker CLI where Docker is the selected runtime
- Docker Compose plugin where required
- Git
- curl
- jq
- openssl
- ca-certificates
- Python/runtime dependencies only where actually required

Dependency installation must be isolated behind platform/package-manager adapters rather than embedded throughout orchestration code.

### Tiny Swarm World installation

The workflow must:

1. run preflight
2. prepare installation directories
3. install/verify dependencies
4. initialize required configuration
5. initialize secrets/credentials through the existing credential boundary
6. configure runtime/orchestrator
7. deploy Tiny Swarm World
8. execute post-install health checks
9. print operator access information and next steps

### Idempotency

Repeated execution must not destroy an existing healthy installation.

Required behavior:

- already installed dependencies are detected
- existing configuration is preserved unless explicitly changed
- repeated execution converges toward the desired state
- destructive changes require explicit operator intent
- partial installation state can be safely resumed where practical

### Architecture boundaries

The shell/bootstrap layer must remain thin.

It should delegate domain/workflow behavior to existing Tiny Swarm World application services wherever possible.

Target separation:

```text
install.sh
   |
   v
Native Linux bootstrap adapter
   |
   v
Installation / reconciliation application service
   |
   +--> Host qualification port
   +--> Package/runtime installation port
   +--> Credential bootstrap port
   +--> Configuration port
   +--> Deployment/orchestrator port
   +--> Verification/evidence port
```

The installer must not become another orchestration hotspot.

### Logging and evidence

The installation must produce sufficient evidence for RC/public-beta qualification.

At minimum:

- detected platform
- preflight result
- dependency verification/install result
- configuration result
- runtime/orchestrator initialization result
- deployment result
- health-check result
- final success/failure summary

Secrets must never be written to logs.

Machine-readable evidence should be emitted where consistent with the existing evidence model.

### Failure handling

On failure:

- exit with a non-zero status
- print the failed stage
- print an actionable diagnostic
- preserve logs/evidence
- avoid silently continuing after a critical failure
- avoid leaving partially written configuration where atomic writes are possible

Rollback behavior must be documented for mutations that cannot safely be made transactional.

## Suggested CLI

```bash
./install.sh
./install.sh --preflight
./install.sh --profile classic
./install.sh --dry-run
./install.sh --verbose
```

Optional future flags may include:

```bash
./install.sh --runtime docker
./install.sh --runtime podman
./install.sh --orchestrator swarm
./install.sh --orchestrator k3s
```

Those options should only be exposed once the corresponding runtime/orchestrator implementations are supported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A native Linux installation can be started through one documented installer entry point.
- [ ] Ubuntu 26.04 LTS is explicitly supported and tested through a clean first installation and safe second run.
- [ ] Native Linux is detected independently from WSL.
- [ ] Preflight runs before mutating the host.
- [ ] Unsupported environments fail fast with actionable diagnostics.
- [ ] Required dependencies are installed or verified deterministically.
- [ ] Installer orchestration is separated from package-manager/platform adapters.
- [ ] Existing Tiny Swarm World application/domain boundaries are reused instead of duplicating orchestration in shell.
- [ ] Installation is idempotent for an already healthy installation.
- [ ] Re-running after an interrupted installation has defined behavior.
- [ ] No credentials or secret values are leaked into logs.
- [ ] The installer generates installation/verification evidence.
- [ ] A successful installation finishes with health checks for the deployed platform.
- [ ] The operator receives URLs/endpoints and next-step information after success.
- [ ] `--preflight` performs validation without installation.
- [ ] `--dry-run` performs no mutating operations.
- [ ] Automated tests cover platform detection and preflight behavior.
- [ ] At least one real native-Linux E2E installation test is documented and reproducible.
- [ ] User/operator documentation describes installation, prerequisites, troubleshooting, and uninstall/recovery behavior.

## Test Matrix

Minimum qualification matrix:

| Environment | Expected |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu 26.04 LTS VM, clean host | Full install succeeds |
| Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, second installer run | No destructive changes; converges successfully |
| Unsupported distribution/version | Clear preflight failure |
| Insufficient disk space | Clear preflight failure |
| Missing sudo/root capability | Clear preflight failure |
| Interrupted installation followed by rerun | Defined recovery/convergence behavior |
| Existing healthy Tiny Swarm World installation | Safe no-op/reconcile behavior |

## Definition of Done

This issue is complete when a clean supported native Linux machine can install Tiny Swarm World through the documented installer, the second run is safe/idempotent, automated tests cover the installer boundaries, and a real native-Linux E2E run produces verifiable evidence suitable for release qualification.

The required live machine for this issue is Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. An existing-platform reconciliation does not establish the clean first-install criterion. Interruption recovery is qualified on an isolated, restorable snapshot. The Ubuntu 24.04 host path remains locally supported but is not substituted for, or claimed as, this issue's Ubuntu 26.04 live qualification.

## Out of Scope

- full K3s implementation
- full Podman runtime implementation
- multi-host provisioning
- DNS server rollout
- replacement of runtime/orchestrator abstractions defined in their dedicated EPICs

These may later consume the installation framework introduced by this issue.

## Purpose

Tiny Swarm World already has a strong hexagonal core with explicit domain/application/infrastructure separation, ports and adapters, automated architecture tests, import-linter contracts, responsibility boundaries and a canonical quality gate.

A source-level architecture audit identified that the remaining structural risk is concentrated primarily at the orchestration edge rather than in the domain/application core. In particular, `src/tiny_swarm_world/__main__.py`, `src/tiny_swarm_world/installer.py` and parts of `src/tiny_swarm_world/infrastructure/composition.py` carry broad responsibilities and are only partially covered by the existing architecture governance.

This EPIC strengthens these boundaries without introducing speculative abstractions or pattern-for-pattern's-sake refactors. The objective is smaller responsibilities, explicit dependency ownership, preserved behavior and machine-verifiable architecture.

## Problem statement

The current architecture rules strongly protect:

- `tiny_swarm_world.domain`
- `tiny_swarm_world.application`
- application ports
- selected responsibility boundaries such as platform, artifacts and deployment

However, root-level orchestration modules are less constrained. This creates a governance blind spot where CLI, installer, composition, filesystem, environment, subprocess, host, credential and presentation responsibilities can accumulate without violating the existing domain/application import contracts.

Current hotspots include:

- `src/tiny_swarm_world/__main__.py`
  - CLI argument parsing
  - workflow registration and routing
  - consent/confirmation handling
  - host/preflight/network dispatch
  - workflow execution orchestration
  - JSON/console presentation
  - direct use of composition builders

- `src/tiny_swarm_world/installer.py`
  - CLI parsing
  - host/runtime detection
  - filesystem and Git probing
  - credential preparation
  - WSL/Windows bridge handling
  - subprocess execution
  - evidence/log handling
  - reset/setup lifecycle orchestration
  - error handling and presentation

- `src/tiny_swarm_world/infrastructure/composition.py`
  - broad wiring responsibilities across multiple capabilities and bounded responsibility areas

The existing architecture tests already acknowledge selected mixed-boundary files. This EPIC turns those known exceptions into a bounded migration target instead of allowing the exception surface to grow.

## Goals

1. Preserve the current domain/application hexagonal architecture and its dependency direction.
2. Make CLI, installer and composition responsibilities explicit and independently testable.
3. Reduce root-level orchestration modules to thin adapters/composition entry points.
4. Extend automated architecture governance so root-level modules cannot become an unrestricted architectural bypass.
5. Reduce the documented mixed-boundary exception set over time.
6. Preserve all current supported Classic behavior, safety controls, consent semantics, evidence contracts and release qualification.
7. Improve readability and change isolation without introducing unnecessary generic frameworks.

## Architecture direction

Target direction, subject to implementation-level Three-Amigos review:

```text
__main__.py
   -> CLI adapter / dispatcher
      -> application use cases / workflow services
         -> application ports
            -> infrastructure adapters

installer entrypoint
   -> installer orchestration application service
      -> explicit ports for host/filesystem/process/evidence/credentials
         -> infrastructure adapters

composition
   -> capability-specific composition modules
      -> one narrow application composition facade where useful
```

Possible CLI decomposition:

```text
adapters/cli/
├── parser.py
├── workflow_registry.py
├── dispatcher.py
├── consent.py
└── renderer.py
```

This is a direction, not a required folder layout. Implementation must prefer the smallest structure that produces clear responsibility ownership.

## Design principles

- Refactor by responsibility, not by file size alone.
- Prefer existing ports and abstractions before creating new ones.
- Create a new port only when a real boundary needs inversion and at least one concrete consumer exists.
- Do not introduce Strategy/Factory/Command/etc. merely to satisfy a design-pattern checklist.
- Keep composition at the system edge.
- Keep domain pure.
- Keep application independent from concrete infrastructure.
- Keep infrastructure adapters focused on technology concerns.
- Keep presentation separate from workflow semantics.
- Preserve explicit live-consent and destructive-operation safeguards.
- No behavior change without an explicit requirement.

## Required audit baseline

Before implementation, produce a source-level responsibility and dependency inventory for at least:

- `src/tiny_swarm_world/__main__.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/installer.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/simple_installer.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/infrastructure/composition.py`
- root-level package modules that import both application/domain and concrete infrastructure

Classify responsibilities as:

- `ENTRYPOINT`
- `PRESENTATION`
- `APPLICATION_ORCHESTRATION`
- `COMPOSITION`
- `INFRASTRUCTURE_ADAPTER`
- `DOMAIN_POLICY`
- `CROSS_BOUNDARY_DEBT`
- `LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY`

For every `CROSS_BOUNDARY_DEBT` item, identify the intended owner and migration path before moving code.

## Work packages

### ARC-01 — Establish architecture and Clean-Code audit baseline
Create a repeatable inventory of large/mixed-responsibility modules, dependency direction, direct technology access, coupling and documented exceptions. Record the desired ownership of each responsibility.

### ARC-02 — Make `__main__.py` a thin CLI entry point
Extract parsing, routing, presentation and command-specific orchestration where this reduces responsibility mixing. Keep the executable entry point focused on bootstrapping and handing control to the CLI adapter.

### ARC-03 — Decompose the installer God-module responsibilities
Separate installer application orchestration from concrete host/filesystem/process/evidence/presentation behavior. Preserve current live-install safety and installation semantics. Avoid rewriting working infrastructure adapters unnecessarily.

### ARC-04 — Modularize composition by capability/boundary
Split broad composition responsibilities where multiple independent capability areas are wired together. Keep one clear composition root while allowing platform/artifacts/deployment/setup/host/network capabilities to be assembled without one ever-growing module.

### ARC-05 — Extend architecture governance to root-level orchestration
Add architecture tests/import contracts that explicitly govern entrypoints, CLI adapters, installer orchestration and composition. Prevent application logic from migrating back into unrestricted root modules.

### ARC-06 — Reduce and govern mixed-boundary exceptions
Review `KNOWN_MIXED_BOUNDARY_FILES` and equivalent documented debt. Every remaining exception must have an owner, rationale and removal/isolation plan. New exceptions require an explicit architecture decision/test update rather than silently accumulating.

### ARC-07 — Verify behavior preservation and regression safety
Run targeted tests plus the canonical quality gate. Ensure supported CLI workflows, installer paths, consent rules, failure states and evidence semantics remain equivalent unless a separately approved requirement changes them.

### ARC-08 — Final independent architecture review
Perform an independent architecture/Clean-Code review against this EPIC's acceptance matrix. Confirm responsibility ownership, dependency direction, testability and remaining debt before closing the EPIC.

## Acceptance criteria

### Architecture
- [ ] Domain remains free of application/infrastructure imports.
- [ ] Application remains free of concrete infrastructure imports.
- [ ] New orchestration behavior is placed in an explicitly owned layer/boundary.
- [ ] Root-level modules cannot act as unrestricted dependency bypasses.
- [ ] CLI presentation does not own infrastructure behavior.
- [ ] Installer application orchestration does not directly own unrelated technology concerns where a stable boundary exists.
- [ ] Composition remains the place where concrete adapters are bound to ports.
- [ ] Broad composition responsibilities are split where independently changeable capability areas exist.

### `__main__.py`
- [ ] `__main__.py` is demonstrably thinner and has one primary responsibility: executable bootstrap/CLI delegation.
- [ ] Workflow parsing/routing/presentation responsibilities have explicit owners.
- [ ] Existing workflow names, safety semantics and exit behavior remain covered by regression tests.

### Installer
- [ ] Installer responsibilities are inventoried before refactoring.
- [ ] Installer orchestration is separable from concrete subprocess/filesystem/host/evidence/presentation concerns.
- [ ] WSL2/native-Linux behavior remains supported according to existing product contracts.
- [ ] Reset/setup ordering, failure propagation and evidence generation remain deterministic.
- [ ] Credential and redaction behavior is not weakened.

### Governance
- [ ] Architecture tests cover the newly established CLI/installer/composition boundaries.
- [ ] The architecture gate fails when prohibited cross-boundary imports or direct technology access are deliberately introduced in protected areas.
- [ ] Known mixed-boundary exceptions are reduced or explicitly justified with owner and follow-up.
- [ ] No new architecture exception is introduced merely to make tests pass.
- [ ] Architecture documentation and ADR/debt documentation reflect the implemented structure.

### Clean Code / maintainability
- [ ] Materially changed modules have clear single primary responsibilities.
- [ ] Naming reflects domain/application/infrastructure intent rather than generic helpers/managers.
- [ ] No new generic abstraction is introduced without a concrete use case.
- [ ] Duplicated orchestration is removed when a canonical owner exists.
- [ ] Dependency injection is used at real technology boundaries rather than for trivial pure functions.
- [ ] Error handling remains explicit and does not hide failure states.

### Verification
- [ ] Targeted architecture tests pass.
- [ ] Targeted CLI and installer regression tests pass.
- [ ] `python3 tools/quality_gate.py quality` passes on the final integrated candidate, or an external/non-code blocker is recorded truthfully according to repository policy.
- [ ] No required RC1/live acceptance result is invalidated by this refactor without rerunning the affected scenario.

## Three-Amigos scenarios

### CLI change
**Given** a developer adds a new CLI command  
**When** the command is implemented  
**Then** parsing/presentation stays in the CLI adapter  
**And** application behavior is implemented behind the appropriate application service/port boundary  
**And** concrete infrastructure is wired through composition.

### Installer capability change
**Given** a new host/install capability requires filesystem or subprocess access  
**When** it is implemented  
**Then** installer orchestration expresses the workflow intent  
**And** concrete technology behavior belongs to an adapter  
**And** the workflow can be tested without executing live infrastructure.

### Architecture regression
**Given** application code directly imports a concrete infrastructure adapter  
**When** the architecture quality gate runs  
**Then** the build fails with an actionable architecture violation.

### Root-level bypass regression
**Given** new application logic is placed into an unrestricted package-root module to avoid layer rules  
**When** architecture tests run  
**Then** the violation is detected or the module must first be explicitly classified and governed.

### Pattern restraint
**Given** existing code can be cleanly decomposed with functions/classes and existing ports  
**When** refactoring occurs  
**Then** no unnecessary generic framework or design pattern hierarchy is introduced solely for stylistic consistency.

## Non-goals

This EPIC must not:

- redesign the domain model without a separate requirement;
- replace the current Classic Docker Swarm behavior;
- implement the future Podman/Kubernetes vision;
- change credential semantics owned by EPIC 02 unless required to preserve existing contracts;
- weaken live-consent, destructive-operation or evidence safeguards;
- broadly rename packages only for aesthetics;
- enforce arbitrary maximum file sizes as an architecture rule;
- introduce patterns solely because a pattern catalog recommends them;
- perform unrelated performance optimization;
- claim live verification without actual live evidence.

## Execution order

1. ARC-01 — establish responsibility/dependency baseline.
2. ARC-05 — define/extend guardrails early so refactoring cannot drift.
3. ARC-02 — thin CLI entry point.
4. ARC-03 — decompose installer responsibilities incrementally.
5. ARC-04 — modularize composition as required by extracted responsibilities.
6. ARC-06 — reduce documented exception surface.
7. ARC-07 — full regression/quality verification.
8. ARC-08 — independent completion audit.

ARC-02/03/04 may proceed in slices after the baseline, but each slice must preserve green architecture and behavioral tests.

## Definition of Done

EPIC 03 is complete when Tiny Swarm World's already strong hexagonal core is matched by equally explicit orchestration-edge boundaries: CLI, installer and composition have clear responsibility ownership; root-level modules are no longer an architectural blind spot; mixed-boundary exceptions are reduced and governed; supported behavior and safety contracts remain intact; and the architecture is enforced by automated tests rather than documentation alone.

The desired outcome is not "more architecture". It is a smaller, clearer and harder-to-accidentally-degrade architecture that remains understandable to human developers and AI-assisted contributors alike.

## Resulting architecture documentation — ARCH-03.21

Tracked by [#364](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/issues/364).
The resulting ownership, dependency, Classic runtime, composition, planning,
configuration/secret/process boundaries, fitness functions and runtime extension
path are documented in
[ARCH-03.21 — Resulting architecture and runtime extension path](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/blob/main/documentation/arc42/05_analysis/arch-03-21-resulting-architecture.md),
linked from the [Developer Manual](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/blob/main/documentation/manuals/developer-manual.md#architecture).

Publication state: [PR #436](https://github.com/MatthiasBurger-Coder/Tiny-Swarm-World/pull/436)
was merged to main on 2026-10-03 (merge commit `9fc5fd439805e0864e4bc6741de6dd08f7746d0a`).
Issue #364 is closed and the guide is available through the links above. CI for
Python 3.12/3.13/3.14, the canonical quality gate and the PR SonarCloud quality
gate all passed. This reference does not mark the remaining EPIC work or live
verification complete.

issues.body:
## Problem

Tiny Swarm World needs three distinct operator workflows:

1. Upgrade the installed **TSW product** to a supported release.
2. Upgrade **individual platform components**, such as Jenkins, Nexus, SonarQube and Portainer.
3. Select **which optional services are installed**, while retaining **Incus/LXC and Portainer as mandatory Classic foundations**.

The completed Classic update work in #297, under #294, provides a supported transition for one existing stack-service image. It must be reused, but it does not establish a complete TSW release upgrade, automatic component-version management, a qualified Portainer upgrade, or arbitrary service selection.

Existing `default` and `service-access` profiles provide fixed service sets. Profile selection alone does not satisfy free selection of optional services.

## Goal

Provide documented commands for release upgrades, component updates and selective installation. Operators can inspect the current state, preview the desired change, apply an explicitly requested operation and verify its result without recreating the complete environment.

Existing configuration, credentials, service identities and persistent data must be preserved except where an explicitly supported migration requires a documented change.

## Scope and ownership

Initial delivery targets the supported **Classic profile: Linux/WSL2 → Incus/LXC → Docker Engine → Docker Swarm**.

This EPIC owns operator workflows and their integration. It reuses existing application ports, adapters, update/recovery logic, configuration contracts and verification infrastructure.

- #297: completed single stack-service image update foundation; reference and reuse, do not reopen its completed scope.
- #294: historical Classic release qualification and acceptance baseline.
- #313: architecture boundaries and orchestration decomposition.
- #314: runtime/orchestrator capability model; align extension contracts without blocking the initial Classic slice on future profiles.
- #318: logical service/version/dependency/lifecycle contracts; coordinate ownership and avoid parallel service models.
- #319: cross-profile release qualification when additional profiles are supported.
- #427: native Linux installation integration and operator entry points.
- #251: wider multi-runtime product vision.

This EPIC does not replace or reopen those trackers. Podman and Kubernetes support requires separate qualified slices.

## Requirements

### LCM-01 — TSW release upgrade

- Inspect the installed TSW release/revision, effective configuration and managed runtime state.
- Resolve an explicit target release using a defined release source and supported upgrade matrix.
- Distinguish the TSW product version from upstream component versions and locally built image versions.
- Validate source and target state, dependency compatibility, host support and required resources before mutation.
- Upgrade product code/package and locked Python dependencies through the supported installation model.
- Apply versioned configuration/state migrations in an explicit order.
- Preserve local overrides, credential-source references, installation identity and persistent service data.
- Keep runtime credentials out of source-control operations, logs and upgrade evidence.
- Use a controlled checkout/package switch; do not overwrite an operator's uncommitted changes or perform an implicit reset.
- Define interruption handling, resumability and recovery for each supported transition.
- Record the actual resulting version and verify the complete installed service selection.

A Git pull or platform reconcile alone must not be reported as a completed product upgrade.

### LCM-02 — Component version discovery and updates

- Report installed and desired component versions, available supported targets and compatibility restrictions.
- Separate upstream versions, image tags and resolved image digests.
- Support one selected service and an explicitly selected batch of installed services.
- Resolve updates through an authoritative component catalog and profile support policy.
- Preview the exact changes, dependency order, restart/availability impact and required migrations.
- Reuse #297 for supported stack-service image transitions.
- Verify deployed task-image convergence and authenticated service behavior after an update.
- Update the persisted desired configuration after a successfully verified transition so later setup/deployment does not silently restore the old image.
- Represent no-op, unsupported, blocked, failed, partial and recovered outcomes explicitly.
- Do not update uninstalled or unselected services implicitly.
- Document stateful-service migration, backup and downgrade restrictions; an image rollback is not a persistent-data restore.

### LCM-03 — Portainer upgrade

Portainer is a mandatory Classic deployment gateway with a separate bootstrap/management lifecycle. Do not assume the generic stack-service update command qualifies its upgrade.

- Inspect the current Portainer version, deployment mode, persistent state and endpoint connectivity.
- Define and test at least one supported source-to-target upgrade.
- Back up the required Portainer state and document compatible recovery boundaries.
- Preserve administrative access, endpoint registration and managed stack ownership.
- Verify the Portainer API and authenticated access, then prove that a managed deployment/update still works.
- Recover without depending exclusively on an unavailable Portainer API.
- Keep Incus host-package upgrades separate from service-image updates; define their ownership and reject unsupported requests explicitly.

### LCM-04 — Selective service installation

- Provide a canonical catalog of service IDs with versions, dependencies, resource requirements and profile support.
- Let operators select optional services through CLI/configuration and persist the resolved selection.
- Keep **Incus/LXC and Portainer mandatory for Classic**; attempts to disable either must fail before mutation with an actionable explanation.
- Treat Incus as a host/provider prerequisite and Portainer as a managed foundation; mandatory status does not imply that the installer already provisions the host Incus daemon.
- Resolve transitive dependencies deterministically. Show dependencies added to the requested selection and the reason for each.
- Document any additional unavoidable dependencies in the current implementation rather than claiming that every remaining service can already be omitted.
- Preflight only the resources, credentials, artifacts and capabilities needed for the resolved service set and mandatory foundations.
- Install, route, display and verify only the resolved services.
- Support a subsequent request to add optional services to an existing installation.
- Preview removals separately; deselection must not silently delete deployed services or persistent data.
- Use the same persisted selection for setup, reconcile, update and verification.
- Do not conflate service selection with runtime/orchestrator selection.

### LCM-05 — Shared operation contract

Every mutating workflow must expose:

1. Current-state inspection and supported-transition validation.
2. A read-only preview with exact targets and planned changes.
3. Explicit live-operation intent through existing consent boundaries.
4. Ordered execution with bounded waits and per-stage results.
5. Post-operation verification tied to the actual deployed state.
6. A documented failure/recovery path and redacted evidence.

A successful command exit, reachable login page or healthy old task alone does not establish update success.

## Proposed CLI contract

These commands describe the intended operator experience. Final spelling must be decided after inspecting the existing CLI; they are **not claims of implemented commands**.

```bash
# Inspect and upgrade the TSW product
tiny-swarm-world version
tiny-swarm-world update --to <tsw-release> --preview
tiny-swarm-world update --to <tsw-release> --live --approve-live

# Inspect component versions and update installed services
tiny-swarm-world services list
tiny-swarm-world services updates
tiny-swarm-world services update --services jenkins,sonarqube --preview
tiny-swarm-world services update --services jenkins,sonarqube --live --approve-live

# Select services for installation
tiny-swarm-world setup run --services jenkins,sonarqube --preview
tiny-swarm-world setup run --services jenkins,sonarqube --live --approve-live
```

Portainer and Incus remain mandatory foundations of the resolved Classic selection. The existing `platform update` contract remains available or receives an explicitly documented compatibility/deprecation path.

## Work packages and execution order

The ten implementation issues below have been created. Their descriptions reference this EPIC, include explicit acceptance IDs and identify dependencies. All ten issues are attached as native GitHub sub-issues of #440, in work-package order. The checklist tracks delivery.

## Implementation issues

- [ ] #441 — [LCM-W01] Inventory lifecycle behavior and define the canonical CLI contract
- [ ] #442 — [LCM-W02] Implement the installation manifest and component version catalog
- [ ] #443 — [LCM-W03] Implement deterministic service selection and dependency planning
- [ ] #444 — [LCM-W04] Integrate selective services into setup and verification
- [ ] #445 — [LCM-W05] Implement supported component discovery and update planning
- [ ] #446 — [LCM-W06] Execute component updates with convergence and recovery
- [ ] #447 — [LCM-W07] Implement a qualified Portainer upgrade and recovery adapter
- [ ] #448 — [LCM-W08] Implement the TSW product release upgrade workflow
- [ ] #449 — [LCM-W09] Qualify selective installation and upgrades on native Linux and WSL2
- [ ] #450 — [LCM-W10] Document lifecycle commands and audit EPIC completion

| Order | Work package | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | LCM-W01 — Inventory and lifecycle ADR | Current commands, installation models, service dependencies, ownership boundaries and canonical CLI decisions |
| 2 | LCM-W02 — Installation manifest and version catalog | Versioned persisted release/component/selection state, support matrix, schema migration and drift detection |
| 3 | LCM-W03 — Service selection planner | Mandatory foundations, dependency resolution, explain/preview and selection persistence |
| 4 | LCM-W04 — Selective setup integration | Selection-aware preflight, deployment, routes, access output, resources and verification; safe addition of services |
| 5 | LCM-W05 — Component discovery and update planning | Supported target discovery, image identity, batch planning and stateful migration requirements |
| 6 | LCM-W06 — Component update execution | Reuse #297; convergence, desired-state persistence, batch failures, retry and recovery |
| 7 | LCM-W07 — Portainer upgrade adapter | Qualified management-gateway upgrade, backup, recovery and post-upgrade deployment proof |
| 8 | LCM-W08 — TSW release upgrade | Supported product/dependency/configuration upgrade with protected overrides and deterministic recovery |
| 9 | LCM-W09 — Host lifecycle qualification | Actual native Linux and WSL2 selective-install/update/recovery evidence |
| 10 | LCM-W10 — Operator documentation and completion audit | README/user-guide commands, Mermaid diagrams, troubleshooting, support limits and requirement-to-evidence review |

Dependencies: W02 follows W01. W03/W05 use W02. W04 follows W03. W06 follows W05. W07 uses the shared update contracts but owns its separate Portainer adapter. W08 consumes the version/migration contracts and completed update boundaries required by its supported release transition. W09 qualifies completed slices; W10 documentation evolves with every slice and closes after W09.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LCM-01: At least one actual supported TSW release upgrade is implemented and verified; product, dependency and configuration changes are distinguished from service-image changes.
- [ ] LCM-02: Installed/supported component versions can be inspected; single-service and selected-batch updates converge and persist their intended configuration.
- [ ] LCM-03: At least one real Portainer upgrade preserves access/endpoints and proves subsequent managed deployment works.
- [ ] LCM-04: A fresh minimal Classic installation and at least two distinct optional-service selections are verified.
- [ ] LCM-04: Disabling mandatory Incus/Portainer foundations or requesting unsupported combinations fails before mutation.
- [ ] LCM-04: Adding an optional service preserves existing service identities, data and effective credentials.
- [ ] LCM-04: Routes, access output and verification match the persisted resolved selection; omitted services are not falsely reported as installed or failed.
- [ ] LCM-05: Every mutating entry point has tested help, argument validation, preview and existing live-consent integration.
- [ ] Repeating a completed operation is a verified no-op; interruption, partial-batch failure and supported recovery have meaningful regression and live coverage.
- [ ] Unsupported stateful downgrade/data-migration requests are rejected explicitly; image rollback is never represented as a data restore.
- [ ] Configuration/runtime drift is visible and cannot produce a false success.
- [ ] Native Linux and WSL2 qualification identifies exact versions, host/profile, service selection, SHA, commands and redacted evidence.
- [ ] Architecture, targeted tests and applicable quality/security gates pass; live results remain separate from unit/mock evidence.
- [ ] Operator documentation explains TSW upgrades, component updates, service selection, mandatory foundations, backups and recovery.
- [ ] A final requirement/architecture/test-evidence review confirms scope and remaining limits before closure.

## Non-goals

- Automatic unattended updates or scheduled updates in the first delivery.
- Arbitrary upgrades to every upstream version without a supported compatibility policy.
- Generic Incus host-package upgrade automation.
- Production/high-availability guarantees.
- Completing Podman/Kubernetes or multi-host support through this EPIC.
- Silent service removal, data deletion, credential rotation or destructive platform recreation.
- A second orchestration engine or parallel logical service schema.

## Execution and completion contract

Follow the repository's current `AGENTS.md`, `QUALITY.md`, `documentation/process/issue-completion-discipline.md` and `documentation/process/verification-state-policy.md` during implementation. Each child issue must define stable requirement IDs, supported transitions, affected services, migration/recovery limits and a requirement-to-evidence matrix.

Live qualification must use explicitly authorized, qualified and recoverable targets. Creation of this EPIC does not authorize infrastructure mutation. Missing, skipped, stale, simulated or inconclusive required live evidence does not count as passed.

Completion requires working operator commands for all three requested areas, qualified Portainer updates, truthful support limits and evidence for preservation/recovery. This EPIC establishes future scope; it does not claim that the new commands are already available.

Work package: **LCM-W04**, execution position 4/10.
Requirements: **LCM-04, LCM-05** from #440.

## Goal

Integrate selective services into setup and verification for the operator workflows defined by #440, reusing the existing hexagonal architecture and lifecycle boundaries.

## Dependencies

- #443 — LCM-W03

## Scope

- Pass one resolved selection through native/WSL setup, preflight, artifact preparation, deployment, routing, access output and verification.
- Require resources/secrets only for selected services and their mandatory dependencies.
- Support adding optional services without recreating an existing healthy platform.
- Retain existing fixed-profile compatibility with documented precedence; distinguish host Incus preparation from managed deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LCM-W04-AC1: A minimal selection and two distinct optional selections have meaningful integration coverage.
- [ ] LCM-W04-AC2: Unselected services are neither deployed nor reported as failed/installed.
- [ ] LCM-W04-AC3: Routes, access output, resource budgets and verification match the persisted selection.

## Validation and evidence

- Map each acceptance ID to the affected architecture contract, meaningful tests and evidence.
- Run targeted tests and applicable QUALITY.md gates. Cover invalid input, read-only preview, no-op and relevant failure paths.
- For mutating workflows verify CLI help, argument validation and existing live-consent behavior.
- Separate unit/mock results from actual live qualification; W09 owns the cross-host matrix and consumes each slice's results.
- Record exact tested SHA, host/profile, product/component versions, resolved service selection, commands, exit codes and redacted before/after observations for live claims.

## Boundaries and completion

Follow current AGENTS.md, QUALITY.md, documentation/process/issue-completion-discipline.md and documentation/process/verification-state-policy.md. Reuse #297 where relevant; coordinate model ownership with #318 and architecture with #313/#314. Do not build a parallel orchestrator, reopen completed #297 scope, or introduce unqualified Podman/Kubernetes behavior.
